questions.question:
A retailer offers the following discount schemes for buyers on an article. Which scheme will be least beneficial to the customer?

i. A discount of 30%.

ii. A discount of 22% followed by a discount of 8%.

iii. Successive discounts of 25% and 5%.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount schemes:

i. A discount of 30%

ii. A discount of 22% followed by a discount of 8%

iii. Successive discounts of 25% and 5%

**Formula used:**

Effective discount for successive discounts = 100 - [(100 - d1) × (100 - d2) / 100]

Where d1 and d2 are the successive discounts.

**Calculation:**

**Scheme i:**

Single discount = 30%

**Scheme ii:**

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - [(100 - 22) × (100 - 8) / 100]

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - [(78 × 92) / 100]

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - 71.76 = 28.24%

**Scheme iii:**

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - [(100 - 25) × (100 - 5) / 100]

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - [(75 × 95) / 100]

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - 71.25 = 28.75%

**Comparison:**

Scheme i = 30%

Scheme ii = 28.24%

Scheme iii = 28.75%

**∴ The least beneficial scheme for the customer is Scheme ii.**

questions.question: In a math exam, two students scored 95, six students scored 90, three students scored 80, and one student scored 50. What was the average score of the class?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Scores: 95 (2 students), 90 (6 students), 80 (3 students), 50 (1 student)

Total students = 2 + 6 + 3 + 1 = 12

**Formula used:**

Average score = (Sum of all scores) / (Total number of students)

**Calculation:**

Sum of scores = (95 × 2) + (90 × 6) + (80 × 3) + (50 × 1)

⇒ Sum of scores = 190 + 540 + 240 + 50 = 1020

Average score = 1020 / 12 = 85

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: The diameter of a hollow hemisphere is 30 cm. Water is filled in it up to its brim. When spherical lead shots each of radius 0.75 cm are dropped into the hemisphere, two-fifth of the water flows out. How many lead shots were dropped into the hemisphere?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the hollow hemisphere (R) = 30 / 2 = 15 cm

Radius of each lead shot (r) = 0.75 cm

Two-fifth of the water flows out

**Formula used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

Number of lead shots = (Volume of water displaced) / (Volume of 1 lead shot)

**Calculations:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

⇒ Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × (15)³

Water displaced = (2/5) × Volume of hemisphere

⇒ Water displaced = (2/5) × (2/3) × π × (15)3

Volume of 1 lead shot = (4/3) × π × r³

⇒ Volume of 1 lead shot = (4/3) × π × (0.75)³

Number of lead shots = Water displaced / Volume of 1 lead shot

⇒ Number of lead shots = [(2/5) × (2/3) × π × (15)3] / [(4/3) × π × (0.75)3]

⇒ Number of lead shots = 1/5 × (15 / 0.75)³ = 1/5 × (20)³ = 1600

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: The radii of the bases of two cylinders and their heights are in the ratio 4 : 3 and 9 : 8, respectively. Find the ratio of their curved surface areas.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radii of the bases of two cylinders are in the ratio 4:3.

The heights of the two cylinders are in the ratio 9:8.

**Formula used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = 2π × radius × height

Ratio of CSA = (r₁ × h₁) : (r₂ × h₂)

**Calculation:**

Let the radii be 4x and 3x, and heights be 9y and 8y respectively.

CSA ratio = (2π × 4x × 9y) : (2π × 3x × 8y)

⇒ CSA ratio = (4 × 9) : (3 × 8)

⇒ CSA ratio = 36 : 24

⇒ CSA ratio = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: A grocer wishes to sell a mixture of two varieties of rice worth ₹48 per kg. In what ratio must he mix the rice to reach this selling price when the cost of one variety of rice is ₹42 per kg and the other is ₹60 per kg?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost of first variety of rice = ₹42 per kg

Cost of second variety of rice = ₹60 per kg

Desired selling price of mixture = ₹48 per kg

**Formula used:**

To find the ratio, we use the rule of alligation:

Ratio = (Price of second variety - Desired price) : (Desired price - Price of first variety)

**Calculation:**

Ratio = (₹60 - ₹48) : (₹48 - ₹42)

⇒ Ratio = ₹12 : ₹6

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: By selling an article for ₹20, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 30%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling price at 10% profit = 110% of CP = ₹20

Desired selling price at 30% profit = 130% of CP

Required increase in selling price = 130% − 110% = 20% of CP

Increase = (20 ÷ 110) × 20 = 400 ÷ 110 = 40 ÷ 11 ≈ ₹3.64

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3.64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹20

Initial Profit₁ = 10%

Required Profit₂ = 30%

**Formula Used:**

CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dfbaf9d50d1c8611216a9d299e29a65cac92471f357055c5434dd078e2b5359a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = (20 × 100) ÷ 110 = 200 ÷ 11

⇒ New Selling Price (SP₂) = (200 ÷ 11) × (130 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP₂ = 260 ÷ 11

⇒ Increase in SP = SP₂ − SP₁

⇒ Increase in SP = (260 ÷ 11) − 20

⇒ Increase in SP = (260 − 220) ÷ 11 = 40 ÷ 11

⇒ Increase in SP = 3.6363... ≈ ₹3.64

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3.64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP) & Selling Price (SP)

Profit occurs when SP is greater than CP. Profit percentage is always calculated on the CP unless otherwise stated. Formula: Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Marked Price (MP) & Discount

Discount is always offered on the MP. Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount. Formula: Discount% = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Direct Multiplication Factor

To directly find the SP when profit percentage is given, simply multiply the CP by the multiplying factor (100 + P%) ÷ 100. For instance, a 30% profit translates to multiplying CP by 1.3.

questions.question: In a circular race of 1 km, two persons X and Y start with the speed of 9 km/h and 18 km/h, respectively, at the same time from the same point. When will they meet for the first time at the starting point when running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of X = 9 km/h

Speed of Y = 18 km/h

Distance of the circular track = 1 km

**Formula used:**

Time taken to meet at the starting point = Distance / Relative Speed

Relative speed when running in the same direction = Speed of Y - Speed of X

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 18 - 9 = 9 km/h

Time taken to meet = Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 1 / 9 hours

⇒ Time = (1 / 9) × 3600 seconds = 400 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: Two athletes X and Y are jogging on a circular path whose circumference is 500 m. Athlete X jogs at a speed of 18 km/h and Y jog at 9 km/h, jogging in opposite directions. The time at which they will meet for the first time is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Athlete X = 18 km/h

Speed of Athlete Y = 9 km/h

Circumference of circular path = 500 m

**Formula used:**

Relative speed = Speed of X + Speed of Y

Time to meet = Distance / Relative speed

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 18 km/h + 9 km/h = 27 km/h

⇒ 27 km/h = 27 × (5 / 18) = 7.5 m/s

Time to meet = Distance / Relative speed

⇒ Time = 500 / 7.5 = 66.66 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: In the first 24 matches, a cricket player averages 60 runs. The overall average for all 32 matches is 80. Determine the average for the last 8 matches.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A cricket player averages 60 runs in the first 24 matches.

Total matches = 32

Overall average = 80

Last 8 matches = Total matches - First 24 matches

**Formula used:**

Total runs = Average × Number of matches

Average for last 8 matches = (Total runs in 32 matches - Total runs in first 24 matches) / 8

**Calculations:**

Total runs in first 24 matches = 60 × 24 = 1440

Total runs in 32 matches = 80 × 32 = 2560

Runs in last 8 matches = Total runs in 32 matches - Total runs in first 24 matches

⇒ Runs in last 8 matches = 2560 - 1440 = 1120

Average for last 8 matches = Runs in last 8 matches / 8

⇒ Average for last 8 matches = 1120 / 8 = 140

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: A vendor bought candies at ₹5 each. At what price must he sell to make 20% profit?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price (C.P.) of one candy = ₹5

Profit percentage = 20%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (S.P.) = C.P. × (1 + Profit% / 100)

**Calculation:**

S.P. = ₹5 × (1 + 20 / 100)

⇒ S.P. = ₹5 × 1.2

⇒ S.P. = ₹6.00

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder is 8580 cm². If the height of the cylinder is 15 cm, then find the diameter (in cm) of the circular base. (Take pi = (22)/(7) )
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 8580 cm²

Height (h) = 15 cm

**Formula used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = 2πrh

Where, r = radius

⇒ r = (8580 × 7) / 660 = 91 cm

Diameter = 2 × r = 2 × 91

⇒ Diameter = 182 cm

questions.question: Arjun mixed three different oils to form a mixture costing ₹25 per litre. The ratio of the three varieties of oil was 1 : 5 : 2. What is the cost (per litre in ₹) of the second variety if the cost per litre of the first and third varieties was ₹20 and ₹30, respectively?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost of the mixture = ₹25 per litre

Ratio of oils = 1 : 5 : 2

Cost per litre of first variety = ₹20

Cost per litre of third variety = ₹30

**Formula used:**

Weighted Average Cost = (Sum of Costs × Respective Quantities) / Total Quantity

**Calculation:**

Let the quantities of oils in the mixture be 1x, 5x, and 2x.

Total quantity = 1x + 5x + 2x = 8x

Weighted Average Cost:

₹25 = [(1x × ₹20) + (5x × Cost of second variety) + (2x × ₹30)] / 8x

⇒ ₹25 = (20x + 5x × Cost of second variety + 60x) / 8x

⇒ ₹25 = (80x + 5x × Cost of second variety) / 8x

⇒ ₹25 × 8x = 80x + 5x × Cost of second variety

⇒ ₹200x = 80x + 5x × Cost of second variety

⇒ ₹120x = 5x × Cost of second variety

⇒ Cost of second variety = ₹120 / 5 = ₹24

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**
